title: Dynamic thresholding and signal-weighted canaries for Optimize evals
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Optimize needs more robust, actionable canary and regression detection for model rollouts. Current binary thresholding across single metrics (e.g., average accuracy delta) produces noisy alerts and frequent false positives when traffic mix changes or when small but high-impact cohorts regress. Problem: teams need deterministic, explainable signals that combine multiple metrics, weight them by customer and SLA impact, and adjust thresholds dynamically based on baseline variance. Goal: define a production-ready eval contract and canary design that uses signal-weighted aggregation, cohort stratification (golden set + targeted adversarial prompts), dynamic thresholds (noise-aware), and a runbook with clear rollback triggers and mitigations.
scope: In-scope: (1) Spec for signal weighting matrix (SLA-weighted signals), (2) Canary sampling plan including golden set, adversarial prompts, and cohort stratification, (3) Dynamic thresholding algorithm and parameters, (4) Acceptance criteria and automated gating rules for A/B canaries, (5) Runbook for triage and rollback actions (model variant fallback, prompt transformation, traffic routing). Out-of-scope: rearchitecting the eval storage pipeline, new instrumentation agents on the runtime (covered by ENG work).
acceptance_criteria: A formal signal-weighting matrix exists that maps metrics (accuracy, safety, latency, hallucination rate, cost-per-token) to a single composite canary score and is documented in Confluence.
Canary sampling plan implemented: 1k golden-set prompts + stratified cohorts (top 10 customers by traffic, random long-tail, adversarial prompts set).
Dynamic thresholding prototype implemented in the eval harness: can compute baseline variance and produce a threshold band (mean ± k*std) per cohort.
Automated A/B gating rule that blocks rollout if composite canary score degradation > configured threshold for two consecutive runs or if any high-priority cohort hits a hard failure condition.
Runbook with step-by-step triage and rollback actions exists, and on-call has run a tabletop drill at least once.
Telemetry and dashboards surfaced in Console: composite score time-series, per-cohort breakdown, and top contributing signals for any alert.
Simulated canary runs (historical replay) show false positive rate <= 5% on past 12 months of traffic when using the new rules vs legacy rules.
success_metrics: Reduction in false-positive canary alerts by >= 60% compared to current binary thresholds
Median time-to-detect regressions for high-impact cohorts <= 10 minutes
Reduction in emergency rollbacks caused by noisy signals by >= 50%
>90% of gated rollouts produce per-cohort explanations that identify top-3 contributing signals
test_plan: 1) Implement eval-harness unit tests for the dynamic thresholding algorithm (edge cases for low-sample cohorts). 2) Replay historical traffic and measure false positive/negative rates. 3) Run controlled A/B experiments with Canary group: new gating vs legacy gating on 10% of internal traffic. 4) Run a tabletop runbook drill with SRE and on-call PM/eng. 5) Validate dashboard alerts and notification routing (Slack/ops).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary-run only): integrate into Optimize eval harness and run daily canaries in non-production for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (Internal A/B): enable gating for 10% internal traffic for 1 week. Phase 3 (Gradual ramp): 10%->50%->100% across non-critical customers over 3 weeks with monitoring windows after each step. Final step: enable for all production rollouts with automatic rollback enabled. Each phase requires sign-off from PM, Eng on-call, and SE/Customer Success for affected accounts.
